business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Advertising Media Arbitrage and Affiliate Lead Gen

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (hybrid federal statute and provincial quasi-constitutional administrative law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 19; Alberta Limited Partnerships Act, RSA 2000, c L-6; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 119.1-119.4; Alberta Partnerships Act, RSA 2000, c P-3.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence) of corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Service Alberta Corporate Registry for an Alberta corporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued in a state party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Alberta registered agent / resident representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the principal's country of origin; if executed in Canada, an Alberta notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for foreign execution); consular legalization required for non-Hague parties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport and proof of residential address of the authorized signatory of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or passport-issuing authority in the signatory's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on issuing jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, Canada's sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, Canadian Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act designated persons, and provincial/domestic politically exposed person (PEP) registers. Initial screening must be completed before name reservation and updated continuously throughout the term of the limited partnership. FinTRAC record-keeping and reporting obligations apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English and French are permitted in Alberta corporate names; all names must be submitted using a NUANS name search report and comprise Latin-alphabet characters. The proposed name must not be confusingly similar to existing trademarks or business names, must not consist solely of descriptive/generic elements, and for a limited partnership must include the prescribed legal element 'Limited Partnership', 'LP' or the French equivalent 'Société en commandite' where applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Director of Partnerships and Corporations / Registrar under Service Alberta, including a new or amended NUANS report and any explanatory submissions distinguishing the rejected name. The request should be filed within 30 days of the rejection notice. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may commence a judicial review application before the Alberta Court of King's Bench.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office only if it is a physical street address in Alberta where legal process can be served and statutory records are maintained and accessible during business hours. However, for an affiliate media-buying limited partnership intended to hold bank accounts with Mercury, Wise, and wire-transfer providers, heavy reliance on a virtual-only registered office may trigger enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny and payment-rail refusals. A physical operational office is therefore strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate likelihood, emerging only upon adverse media coverage, high-risk PEP involvement, or regulatory complaint. Estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation: 5-10%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary tariff and apostille/consular fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal counsel / law firm filing the appeal with Service Alberta

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), as amended; the Business Corporations Act does not apply to the limited partnership itself.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Alberta Registrar of Companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; initial capital contribution is fixed by the limited partnership agreement and must be accurately stated in the Declaration, as a false statement may expose the general partner to liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous written consent of the board of directors of the corporate general partner of the Limited Partnership, that: (1) the subscription of initial limited partner interests and related capital contributions is approved, and capital accounts shall be recorded; (2) the registered office be established at the Alberta address identified in the Declaration of Limited Partnership and that address is adopted for service of process; (3) [Name] is appointed designated officer for registry filings and process; and (4) the officers are authorized to execute all registration forms, tax program applications and bank account documentation. This resolution is effective immediately and binds the Limited Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (NUANS name search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct NUANS name search for the proposed limited partnership name. The name must include the statutory designator 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'. Compare existing corporate and LP registrations and obtain a name search report. Submit a name reservation or hold request if offered by the registry process.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses the name, select a distinctive alternative and resubmit, or file a consent from the conflicting name holder to permit the use of the proposed name; a Name Reservation search may also be re-run with revised keywords.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (pre-filing and documentary review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Declaration of Limited Partnership in the prescribed registry format. Include the full legal name, Alberta registered office address, general partner particulars, limited partners' liability restrictions and capital contribution summary. Have the general partner execute the declaration and obtain consents from all limited partners.
required_dossiers: Consent of general partner to act
Contact list and citizenship/residency statements for limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the declaration for deficiencies, amend and re-execute the declaration; an administrative correction or supplemental filing can cure typographical or address-related errors before registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Statutory Registration and Pay Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online filing through authorized corporate registry agent or in-person service counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership to the Alberta Corporate Registry together with the applicable registration fee. Obtain the Certificate of Registration and any stamped copy of the declaration. Ensure the general partner's directors execute the online filing authorization if using a service provider.
required_dossiers: Name search report or reservation confirmation
Identity documents (driver's licence/passport) for general partner signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond with corrected information and consent letters within 30 days; if late or deficient, withdraw and refile the declaration to avoid accumulated penalties and adverse trade registry remarks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Registered Office and Appoint Officer for Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) and Alberta Justice / service agent records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the Declaration states a physical Alberta registered office (not a post-office box alone) for service of process. Adopt a board resolution confirming the office and designate an officer or registered agent to receive legal process. If the registered office changes after filing, submit the registry amendment notice.
required_dossiers: First board resolution of the corporate general partner
Registered address consent from landlord/office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the office address is rejected because it is not a physical location, procure a registered office address and file an address correction; if the officer declines service, appoint a substitute agent and file an amendment to the registry record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Canada Revenue Agency and Alberta Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration for provincial program accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the CRA Business Registration Online portal to register the Limited Partnership for a Business Number (BN), GST/HST program account, payroll (RP) account if employees are anticipated, and related Alberta corporate tax program accounts where the limited partnership has Canadian-source income. The corporate general partner should be identified as the representative and managing partner.
required_dossiers: Corporate general partner's Certificate of Incorporation
CRA BN online access / representative authority form
Limited partnership agreement and general partner resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA delays the BN due to incomplete partnership information, submit the partnership agreement and declaration copy to CRA, complete the partnership identification questionnaire, and follow up through the CRA business enquiries line; corrections are processed administratively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Municipal Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs / local municipal licensing office (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton as applicable); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety for workplace clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain registered records, minute book and limited partner registers. If a physical office or commercial space is opened, obtain the municipal business licence and occupancy permit. Complete OHS workplace hazard assessment and, if required, fire safety inspection before commencing digital advertising operations and affiliate media buying.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and limited partner register
OHS registration form and fire safety checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing is refused, appeal to the local development authority or apply for a zoning variance; if OHS clearance is not issued, correct workplace non-conformities and schedule a re-inspection within the municipal or provincial review period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs / Service Alberta, acting with Alberta Environment and Protected Areas where physical premises trigger environmental assessment requirements
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business / Occupancy License (municipal) and, where applicable, Alberta Environment approval for commercial premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-only digital advertising and affiliate media buying does not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment or registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; a Class 1 approval may be triggered only if material physical works or effluent-generating operations are established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge expected; office wastewater is governed by municipal sewer discharge bylaws. VOC-emitting office equipment and appliances must meet applicable Alberta Occupational Exposure Limits and municipal air quality bylaws. Electronic waste, batteries and digital hardware must be disposed through registered recyclers under Alberta's Recycling Regulation / zero-waste programs, with no uncontrolled landfill or open burning.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Alberta Fire Code officer or municipal fire authority; structural load inspection / occupancy permit issued by municipal building services; workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act confirming there are no uncontrolled electrical, heat or ergonomic hazards in the licensed office and server/storage areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax, GST/HST and payroll; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial corporate tax. Official portals: www.cra.gc.ca and www.alberta.ca/tax
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities including Limited Partnerships obtain a Business Number (BN) directly from the CRA. Foreign entities register for a GST/HST number if they have a permanent establishment in Canada or make taxable supplies therein exceeding the registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian partnerships are automatically pass-through entities with no check-the-box election available; hybrid mismatch elections may apply under domestic anti-avoidance rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered GST/HST persons must issue tax invoices for taxable supplies. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory via CRA My Business Account; real-time digital reporting applies to larger registrants.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services performed outside Canada qualify for zero-rated GST/HST treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may result in reassessment; penalties for fraudulent zero-rating claims include fines up to 50% of the tax or more, plus interest and potential criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with supervisory coordination by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federally regulated banks, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border funds monitoring; the Department of Finance Canada holds exchange policy jurisdiction. Canada requires no exchange-control approval for any FX transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully liberalised, freely floating currency regime with complete current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is freely tradable and no statutory restrictions exist on profit remittance, foreign-currency bank balances, or dividend/partnership distribution repatriation. Structural friction arises exclusively from tax and reporting mechanics: (i) distributions by the Alberta limited partnership to non-resident limited partners must be split into return of capital (exempt from withholding) and Canadian-source income (Part XIII withholding of 25%, generally reduced to 15% or 0% under the Canada-US tax treaty where the US partner provides a valid IRS Form W-8BEN-E and meets treaty-limitation tests); (ii) every cross-border electronic fund transfer of CAD 10,000 or more is automatically reported to FINTRAC without prior authorization; and (iii) the bank applies Enhanced Due Diligence ('Medium-Risk Enhanced' tier for performance media buying) to each capital call, requiring source-of-funds evidence before value is credited.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirement, statutory repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds in Canada. A resident business may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in USD or any convertible currency. Legal obligations are limited to: (a) preserving ledgers and supporting documents under Income Tax Act s. 230; (b) computing all Canadian tax attributes in CAD functional currency; and (c) reporting electronic funds transfers over CAD 10,000 to FINTRAC. For the media-buying model, USD receipts from US affiliate networks should be swept daily from payment gateways into a USD operating account and periodically converted at a board-approved trigger rate to stabilise CAD net income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Capital Escrow Account and CAD Operational Treasury Account
CAD Operational Account with integrated US TD Bank sweep line
CAD/USD Operational Accounts with dedicated US correspondent clearing network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as primary treasury; Medium as a settlement sub-rail. Wise Business and Payoneer hold Canadian Money Service Business (MSB) registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and can serve as low-value disbursement rails for overseas publishers, but they must never concentrate LP capital because balances are unsecured and not covered by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). Mercury (U.S. fintech) is practically infeasible: the Alberta LP without a U.S. EIN and U.S. registered address will normally fail Mercury's entity-nexus onboarding; usage of Mercury should be discontinued in favour of a Tier-1 Schedule I bank with a U.S. correspondent. A dual-rail structure (Tier-1 concentration account + Wise batch payout) is the recommended compliant topology.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted only by exception. For the Alberta LP whose General Partner and ultimate beneficial owners reside outside Canada, Tier-1 banks will condition account opening on either (a) an in-person meeting at a Canadian branch (Calgary, Edmonton, or Vancouver) with the GP's authorised signatory, or (b) a live video interview supported by notarised/certified corporate documents, a Canadian lawyer's certificate of incumbency, and a registered agent appointment in Alberta. For a 'Medium-Risk Enhanced' media-buying profile, a minimum of one in-person 'meet-and-confirm' session is the prudent baseline assumption; some banks additionally require the GP to maintain a Canadian correspondence address and a designated Canadian-resident compliance contact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding > 25% economic or voting interest with no Canadian physical management nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS/CBCR tax self-certification per partner; source-of-wealth letter issued by an audited regulated bank; 24-month personal/entity bank statements; executed capital call schedule; certified Limited Partnership Agreement; Canadian registered office lease; and Alberta Corporate Registry certificate confirming the general partner's registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-ticket cross-border payments to foreign affiliates and publishers matching a money-laundering pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master media-buying agreements with each counterparty; granular payout schedule mapped to performance dashboards (Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Taboola, affiliate network logs); sample invoices with unique order identifiers; sell-side client contracts; monthly reconciliation of clicks/lead events to payouts; named beneficial-ownership registers for publisher counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party USD injection from a U.S. aggregating LLC rather than directly from the named limited partner's account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices matching expected amounts; contribution schedule; partner resolution authorising the funding path; sworn declaration that the funds belong solely to the partner and contain no client money; wire authorisation from the partner's U.S. bank; and a legal opinion characterising the US LLC as a disregarded funding conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital EMI (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury) presented as the principal operational treasury
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tier-1 bank confirmation as the primary concentration account; written designation of the EMI as a payment-only sub-rail; copy of the EMI's FINTRAC MSB registration; daily sweep reconciliation from EMI to Tier-1; contractual cap on EMI float; and a monthly consolidated treasury report delivered to the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advertiser or publisher counterparties domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening output demonstrating no match; per-counterparty due diligence file; contractual AML default and termination clauses; approved settlement-country matrix; ad-platform geolocation proof confirming traffic originates from the US, EU, UK, AU, CA, NZ corridors; and external counsel sign-off where any exception is requested.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) The partner's originating U.S. bank issues a SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian bank's correspondent (e.g., RBC's U.S. branch or TD Bank USA); (2) field 50K must match the partner's exact legal name and field 59 must carry the LP's legal name and the designated account number; (3) field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'LP capital contribution - Schedule [X] - Partner Ref [XXX]'; Canada has no statutory purpose code system, but the compliance officer maps this narrative to the bank's internal capital-receipt taxonomy; (4) a PDF of the capital call notice must be emailed to the relationship manager before the wire to fast-track Enhanced Due Diligence; (5) USD wires should clear through the bank's U.S. clearing arm to avoid correspondent holds; (6) FINTRAC EFT reporting for values equal to or above CAD 10,000 is automatic and requires no pre-approval; and (7) where cumulative inbound capital exceeds CAD 50,000 in a 12-month window, the source-of-wealth dossier must already reside in the KYC file before value is released.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail matrix: (a) Domestic CAD business-to-business payments use Payments Canada's Lynx high-value wire system for urgent transfers and the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch ACH; (b) cross-border USD settlements to media vendors and ad exchanges use SWIFT MT103 with gpi end-to-end tracking through the Tier-1 bank's U.S. correspondent, with MT202 cover used only for bank-to-bank reimbursement; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 remain available for large inventory commitments but are rarely used in performance media arbitrage because documentary mismatch risk exceeds benefit; (d) low-value publisher payouts are executed through Wise batch API as a named sub-rail, each payout matched against an affiliate invoice and a platform proof-of-performance report, with daily sweeps back to the Tier-1 concentration account; and (e) all disbursements operate under a two-person maker-checker control with a standing rule that no payment issues to any counterparty lacking a completed publisher-vetting file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards with tenor up to 24 months under a Tier-1 ISDA/CSA, collateralised per the Credit Support Annex - fully permissible and recommended.
FX swaps for rolling liquidity management and CAD/USD balance repositioning - fully permissible under an approved FX line.

Purchased CAD/USD currency options (calls and puts) for asymmetric protection of non-resident distributions and capital repatriation - permissible with premium prefunding; writing naked options requires an approved credit line and is not recommended.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) for committed treasury-scale expenditure - permissible with OSFI-regulated counterparties and a negotiated CSA.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted-currency corridors (CNY, INR, BRL, and other non-convertible settlement currencies) to hedge foreign affiliate receivables - permissible with a licensed global dealer, subject to a board-approved hedging policy and enhanced AML narrative on underlying trade flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of the registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to $500, potential administrative strike-off after 30 days

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit required for limited partnerships under Alberta law

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial owners and partner ownership changes required; notifications for transfers within 15 days

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: No entity-level income tax applies to a limited partnership (CA_LP); income is allocated to partners. Combined headline corporate rate in Alberta for corporate partners: federal 15% + Alberta provincial 8% = 23%. For Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners qualifying for the small business deduction, the combined rate is reduced to 11% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (as of 2024).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for advertising/media-buying activities. Available incentives include: (i) CCPC small business deduction for Canadian-resident corporate partners, (ii) refundable SR&ED investment tax credits of up to 35% on qualifying eligible R&D in Canada, and (iii) accelerated capital cost allowance for eligible computing/audio-visual and digital media assets used directly in the partnership's commercial activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) - T5013 Summary and individual T5013 slips, filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through approved electronic filing software (EFILE/XML) or by paper; partner-level tax returns (T1 for individual partners, T2 for corporate partners) are filed separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the partnership files one T5013 return each fiscal period. Partner-level income tax and tax instalments are annual/quarterly depending on the partner's method of assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 return is due within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 year-end). A corporate partner's T2 Corporation Income Tax Return is due within six months after the corporate taxation year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Partnership Business Number (BN) and Legal Name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the limited partnership, CRA business number, and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the partnership BN and provide the name, address, and telephone number of the Canadian-resident general partner or agent authorized to accept service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total partnership net income/loss for Canadian tax purposes and each partner's allocated share under the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify Canadian-source business income attributed to non-resident partners; include the allocated share in a manner that permits the non-resident partner to report Part I tax and tracks any Part XIII withholding exposure for passive amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 22 - Partner Identification and Country of Residence
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each partner: full legal name, address, taxpayer identification number (TIN), percentage of profit/loss sharing, and country of tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foreign TIN (e.g., US EIN, UK UTR) and, if treaty relief is claimed, attach a valid Certificate of Residence / TRC issued by the partner's home tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013: CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; for a subsequent or knowing failure, CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000. Failure to issue T5013 slips: CAD 25 per slip per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500). Late T2 filing for corporate partners: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for taxable dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an income tax treaty. For an LP, ordinary profit distributions allocated as business income are not subject to Part XIII withholding if the non-resident partner is taxable under Part I on the Canadian-source business income; however, amounts paid by the LP to non-residents that are characterized as dividends, management fees, interest, royalties, or rental income are subject to the appropriate 25% statutory withholding regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the Canadian payer must obtain a complete and signed Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the non-resident recipient's home tax authority before remittance, and retain it in the payer's records. If the recipient is an individual, corporation, or partnership, CRA forms NR301/NR302/NR303 may also be required depending on residency status. Where the full statutory amount was withheld because treaty relief was not established before payment, the non-resident may apply to the CRA for a refund under subsection 227(6) of the Income Tax Act within the applicable statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for interest (subject to specific exemptions, including arm's-length interest payments to unrelated payees in certain circumstances) and 25% for royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly apply: under the Canada-US treaty, interest is generally subject to 0% withholding in respect of arm's length dealings or 15% in certain non-arm's length or contingent interest cases, and royalties are subject to 10% (including advertising or copyright-related licensing royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for mandatory filing of Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's-Length Transactions with Non-Residents); contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File/Master File) is expected for controlled transactions of any materiality when CRA audits; Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta and Canada have no Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to those in zero-tax jurisdictions. Substance is instead enforced through: (i) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under section 245 of the Income Tax Act, (ii) transfer-pricing recharacterization under section 247, and (iii) treaty anti-abuse / limitation-on-benefits clauses. The LP must maintain demonstrable commercial substance: physical office or management presence in Alberta, active digital media buying operations, real client contracts, payroll, and operating bank accounts in the entity's own name.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully making false statements in T5013/T2 returns, fabricating media-buying expenses, understating revenue, or diverting Canadian-source commissions to an offshore shell corporation controlled by the same principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under subsection 239(1) of the Income Tax Act: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment (up to 2 years on summary conviction). Civil consequences: full reassessment plus interest, gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under subsection 163(2), and suspension of CRA programs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the LP is jointly and severally liable for all partnership obligations and civil tax penalties. A corporate general partner's directors and officers may be personally assessed for unremitted source deductions or Part XIII withholdings under director liability provisions; upon laying of criminal charges, travel bans, border flags, and personal seizure orders can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking media-buying fees or lead-generation commissions to a related non-resident service company that has no employees, no premises, no real business activity, and no independent commercial purpose, resulting in Canadian profit being shifted offshore at non-arm's-length prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing reassessment under subsection 247(2) plus penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment under subsection 247(3). If the arrangement is also abusive, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under section 245 can nullify the tax benefit and impose a penalty equal to 25% of the benefit, plus interest and compounding late payment penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner can be liable for the LP's transfer-pricing penalties where they knowingly participated in or accepted the artificial arrangement. General partners are jointly and severally liable for all tax debts of the partnership, and a non-resident director may face travel restrictions, asset freezes, and personal civil enforcement during a CRA or Public Prosecution Service investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Mercury ACH, wire transfers, or Wise payment rails to move high volumes of cross-border money for foreign clients while failing to (i) maintain beneficial ownership and transaction records, (ii) perform due diligence on ultimate principals, (iii) report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC, or (iv) register as a Money Services Business where payment-processing activity crosses the MSB threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), administrative monetary penalties can reach up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for entities and significant penalties for individuals; criminal enforcement for knowingly failing to report or obstructing FINTRAC can result in imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and the general partner can be personally named in FINTRAC penalty proceedings where they directed or acquiesced in AML breaches. Federal enforcement may also lead to seizure orders, restrictions on international wire transfers, removal of business banking relationships, and travel bans pending criminal trial.
